back: Producing in ways that use resources efficiently and protect the environment so production can continue long term.
Renewable: replaced naturally (solar, wind, replanted forests). Non-renewable: cannot be replaced (coal, oil, minerals).
Renewable energy, using fewer resources, reducing waste, reusing, recycling, environmentally friendly products and packaging.
Reusing: using an item again in its existing form (returnable bottles). Recycling: processing it into new material.

front: Advantages of sustainability for a business?
back: Lower long-run costs, better reputation, access to customers who demand standards, avoiding fines, secure supplies.

front: Disadvantages of sustainability for a business?
back: High initial costs, sometimes higher unit costs, slow savings, competition from cheaper unsustainable rivals.

front: Sustainable use of land and water?
back: Crop rotation, contour ridges, controlled grazing, drip irrigation, rainwater harvesting, no pollution of rivers.

front: Sustainable use of forests and wildlife?
back: Replant and cut only regrowth, woodlots, efficient stoves; protect habitats, prevent poaching, community tourism income.
